hook.line: Tomás looks at the contract he signed and can only say what everyone says too late. Spanish has short exclamations for wishes and regrets, and they sound like they are bursting out of you.
hook.en: I wish I'd never signed it!

examples.en: I wish I'd never signed it!

rule:
Spanish can drop the "I wish" and just exclaim the wish itself.

For the past, which can no longer change, use *hubiera* + the past participle after *si*, *ojalá* or *quién*: *¡Si lo hubiera sabido!*, *¡Quién hubiera estado ahí!*

For something you want now, use the plain wish form: *¡Si al menos llamara!* Adding *al menos* gives the sense "at least".

*¡Quién lo hubiera dicho!* is a fixed way to say "who would have thought it", and it is about surprise, not regret.

No sentence follows. These exclamations stand alone, and the feeling carries the rest.
smallPrint: Teachers call these exclamative wishes: the pluperfect subjunctive (*hubiera* + participle) for unreal past, the imperfect subjunctive (*llamara*) for unreal present.

options: If only Rosa had been here!
I hope I never sign it!
I wish I never signed it now!
I wish I'd never signed it!
I wish I were there now!

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *¡Si lo ___ sabido!* (*hubiera* or *habría*) If only I'd known!
yourTurn.why: After *si*, Spanish uses *hubiera* + participle for a past wish, not *habría*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *¡Si al menos ___!* (*llamara* or *hubiera llamado*) Right now you want him to call: If only he'd call!
yourTurn.why: The wish is about now, so you need the plain wish form: *llamara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Who would have thought it!
yourTurn.why: *Quién* + *lo hubiera dicho* is the fixed way to show surprise.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I wish I'd never signed it!
Say, about us: If only we'd arrived earlier!
yourTurn.why: *Hubiéramos* is the form for *we*, then the participle *llegado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Move it to the past: *¡Si al menos llamara!* becomes If only he'd called!
yourTurn.why: For something already over, *llamara* becomes *hubiera llamado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about you: *¡Si hubiéramos llegado antes!* becomes If only I'd arrived earlier!
yourTurn.why: For *I*, the form is *hubiera*, with the same participle.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *si* use *hubiera*; *habría* belongs to the other half of the sentence.
Almost. After *si* the wish uses the form ending in *-ara*, not the *-ía* one.
After *hubiera* you need the participle, *sabido*, not the infinitive.
Almost. *¿Quién lo dijo?* asks who said it; the exclamation needs *hubiera dicho*.

personal: Think of one thing you regret and one thing you wish for right now. Say them with *¡Si hubiera…!* and *¡Si al menos…!*
